title: Payload-aware span bucketer with sparse-attention prefill scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce wasted padding and improve end-to-end token throughput for mixed-length workloads by introducing a payload-aware span bucketer that uses per-request payload metadata to form micro-batches and a sparse-attention-aware prefill scheduler to gate kernel selection during prefill vs decode phases. Motivation: our current length-driven bucketing still pads excessively for workloads with small high-variance prefixes (e.g., chat histories + long code blocks). By combining payload signals (content-type, expected continuation length, presence of code blocks) with seqlen clustering we can form micro-batches that better align with optimized kernels and selective attention kernels, reducing total padded tokens and improving overall throughput and cost. This ticket covers design, simulation, and a first-pass implementation in the prefill scheduler + runtime hints to kernel selector.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by runtime and kernel teams
Simulation shows >=18% reduction in padded tokens on benchmark suite A (chat+code mix)
End-to-end hosted p50 decode latency unchanged or improved, p95 < 5% regression
PR with scheduler + kernel-hint plumbing merged and e2e perf tests added
Canary rollout plan annotated in console and rollback knob exists
implementation_notes: Add payload classifier hook in request ingestion that annotates request metadata with: content_type, expected_completion_range, has_long_literal_block
Extend seqlen bucketer to accept payload vectors and compute a distance metric that weights payload similarity higher than absolute seqlen for short prefixes
Introduce 'attention_profile' hint: {dense, sparse-prefill, sparse-decode} as a string flag attached to batch keys
Modify kernel selection API: accept attention_profile hint, prefer sparse-kernel variants for prefill if flagged
Place scheduler changes behind runtime feature flag 'payload_bucketer_v1' and add telemetry hooks to compare baseline vs new bucketing
Keep decode path conservative initially: only apply sparse attention kernels for decode when model ACL lists kernel-compatibility and tests pass
comments: 2026-02-11 Marco Ruiz: Kickoff meeting notes — agreed to scope to prefill bucketing first, decode-only changes deferred unless safe kernel exists.
2026-02-18 Sasha Kim: Ran offline sims on chat+code dataset; early results show ~22% pad reduction when content_type is used as a clustering feature; variance high on very short requests.
2026-02-23 Aisha Patel: Design doc uploaded and reviewers requested (runtime, kernels, QA). Key open question: how to surface misclassification-induced tail latency?
2026-02-26 Marco Ruiz: Prototype scheduler implemented in staging with feature flag. Initial e2e smoke looks good — small p50 improvement on batch decode throughput.
2026-02-28 QA Bot: Added automated crash-fuzz test for attention_profile plumbing — no regressions after 1000 runs.
decisions: Use lightweight payload classifier based on heuristics + small TF model rather than full semantic encoder to keep ingestion overhead <0.2ms/request
Stage rollout: simulation -> staging canary (1%) -> regional canary (10%) -> global; enable rollback by toggling 'payload_bucketer_v1' flag
Prefer sparse prefill kernels when attention_profile == 'sparse-prefill' and kernel compatibility table indicates no loss of correctness
Do not enable sparse-attention kernels for decode by default until we have 2 weeks of canary telemetry and kernel-level float-precision regression tests pass
